In addition, there generally is no clear scalar choice for the policy variable x. If policy were framed in terms of strict targets for the money supply, for a specific measure of banking sector reserves, or for a particular short-term interest rate, then the definition of x might be straightforward. In general, however, several candidate measures of monetary policy will be available, all depending in various degrees on both policy actions and nonpolicy disturbances. What constitutes an appropriate candidate for x, and how x depends on nonpolicy disturbances, will depend on the operating procedures the monetary authority is following as it implements policy.
